## Concurrency / Async Model

**Model used:** {e.g. Kotlin Coroutines + Flow / JavaScript async-await + Promises / Python asyncio / Swift async-await / C# Task + async-await / Go goroutines + channels}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. All async operations in ViewModels use `viewModelScope.launch` — never `GlobalScope`}
- {e.g. `suspend` functions must be called from a coroutine scope or another suspend function}
- {e.g. Use `Dispatchers.IO` for network and disk I/O; `Dispatchers.Main` for UI updates}
- {e.g. Never block the main thread — all I/O must be off the main thread}
- {e.g. Use `Flow` for streams; `suspend fun` for one-shot async operations}
- {e.g. In tests, replace dispatchers with `TestCoroutineDispatcher` / `StandardTestDispatcher`}

## Null Safety / Type Safety

**Null safety model:** {e.g. Kotlin null safety — all types non-null by default / TypeScript strict null checks / Swift optionals / C# nullable reference types enabled}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. Never use `!!` — always handle null explicitly with `?.`, `?:`, or `requireNotNull()`}
- {e.g. Nullability of domain models: domain types are non-null; DTOs may use nullable fields during mapping}
- {e.g. Use `@NonNull` / `@Nullable` annotations on public Java APIs if Java modules exist}
- {e.g. TypeScript: do not use `as` type assertions unless you have explicit runtime validation}

## Error Propagation

**Strategy:** {e.g. `Result<T>` / `Either<Error, T>` / Exceptions / `Option<T>` / Error union types / `(value, error)` tuples}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. Repository layer wraps all I/O in `runCatching {}` and returns `Result<T>`}
- {e.g. ViewModel unwraps `Result` and maps to sealed `UiState` variants}
- {e.g. Never propagate raw exceptions to the UI layer}
- {e.g. Log at the point of origin with full context; do not re-log when re-throwing}

## Memory Management

**Model:** {e.g. JVM GC (no manual management) / ARC in Swift (watch for retain cycles) / Go GC / Rust ownership + borrow checker / C++ RAII}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. In Compose: avoid capturing `ViewModel` references in long-lived lambdas — use stable callbacks}
- {e.g. In Swift: use `[weak self]` in closures captured by async operations to prevent retain cycles}
- {e.g. In Rust: prefer owned types in public APIs; use `&str` / `&[T]` only for read-only borrows}

## Logging & Observability

**Logging library:** {e.g. Android Logcat (Log.d/i/w/e) / Timber / SLF4J + Logback / structlog / Serilog / zerolog}  
**Log levels in use:** {e.g. DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR — VERBOSE only in local dev}  
**Structured logging:** {e.g. JSON format in production / key=value pairs}  
**Crash reporting:** {e.g. Firebase Crashlytics / Sentry / Datadog}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. Never log PII (names, emails, health data) — log only IDs}
- {e.g. All exceptions must be logged at ERROR level with full context before re-throwing or converting to UiState.Error}
- {e.g. Use log tags consistently — one tag per class, usually the class name}

## Documentation

**Docstring style:** {e.g. KDoc for public APIs / JSDoc for TypeScript public exports / Google-style docstrings for Python / XML doc comments for C# public APIs}

**Rules:**
- {e.g. All `public` and `internal` functions must have KDoc / JSDoc describing params, return, and thrown exceptions}
- {e.g. `@param` and `@return` tags are required for non-trivial functions}
- {e.g. TODOs in code must include the ticket ID: `// TODO(BUG-101): remove after migration`}

## Framework-Specific Rules

> Additional rules specific to the primary framework used in this project.

### {Framework Name} — {e.g. Jetpack Compose / React / Django / SwiftUI / ASP.NET Core}

- {e.g. Compose: composable functions must be side-effect free — use `LaunchedEffect` / `SideEffect` for effects}
- {e.g. Compose: use `key()` in lazy lists to ensure correct recomposition}
- {e.g. React: prefer functional components with hooks — no class components}
- {e.g. React: co-locate state as close to its consumer as possible before lifting}
- {e.g. Django: use class-based views for CRUD resources; function-based for one-off endpoints}
- {e.g. ASP.NET: use minimal API or controller pattern consistently — do not mix}
